source.section: Schedule SB (PDF page 1) and its Instructions: line 4 (SB Instructions PDF page 2); line 16 and its Caution (SB Instructions PDF page 7; Publication 126 PDF page 8 section 4.E(1); Publication 106 PDF page 4 section 3.C(1)); Form 1 lines 1-12 (Form 1 PDF page 1); Form 1 Instructions PDF page 15 line 8 and lines 10a-10b (PDF pages 15-16), PDF pages 35-37 2025 Standard Deduction Table (row named in worked), PDF page 15 line 12 with the PDF pages 38-43 Tax Table and PDF page 44 Tax Computation Worksheet; tax figured from the 2025 Tax Rate Schedules, Publication 106 PDF pages 6-7

worked: Single, 70: IRA distributions 18,000, interest 30,000, Social Security 30,000. Line 16 subtracts all 18,000 of IRA income (under the 24,000 cap); line 4 removes the taxable Social Security. Claiming line 16 gives up every Wisconsin credit; the projection models none. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = ira distribution (you) 18,000.00 + interest 30,000.00 + taxable Social Security 25,500.00 (gross 30,000.00; provisional income 48,000.00 + half of 30,000.00 = 63,000.00; taxable Social Security 25,500.00) = 73,500.00. Federal taxable income = 73,500.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 + 1 x 2,000.00 = 55,750.00; the federal senior deduction is ignored. Form 1 line 1 federal AGI 73,500.00; line 2 Schedule I adjustments 0.00; line 3 73,500.00; line 4 additions 0.00; line 5 73,500.00. Schedule SB: line 4 Social Security adjustment = 25,500.00; line 16 retirement income subtraction: qualifying income you (age 70): IRA 18,000.00 = 18,000.00; smaller of 18,000.00 and the 24,000.00 cap = 18,000.00; line 50 total 43,500.00. Schedule SB line 17: federal AGI 73,500.00 is not less than 15,000.00, so no 5,000 subtraction. Form 1 line 6 43,500.00; line 7 Wisconsin income = 73,500.00 - 43,500.00 = 30,000.00. Line 8 standard deduction, 2025 Standard Deduction Table (Form 1 Instructions PDF page 35), row 30,000 to less than 30,500, column Single: 12,276.00 (printed row, at least / less than / single / joint / separate / head of household: 30,000 / 30,500 / 12,276 / 24,707 / 8,595 / 15,111). Line 9 = 30,000.00 - 12,276.00 = 17,724.00. Line 10a 1 x 700 = 700.00; line 10b 1 x 250 = 250.00; line 10c 950.00. Line 11 taxable income = 17,724.00 - 950.00 = 16,774.00. Line 12 tax, Schedule A (single) as numbers: 3.5% x 14,680.00 = 513.80 + 4.4% x 2,094.00 = 92.136; total 605.936, rounded once to 605.94. The Tax Table row 16,700 to 16,800 (PDF page 39) gives 605; expected keeps the schedule. Credits (lines 13-20, 30-35): none modelled; 0.00. State income tax 605.94.
accepted_approximations: The projection always takes the 24,000/48,000 subtraction for a person 67 or older, never the Wisconsin credits it bars (see not_modelled); a household whose credits are worth more would skip it.
